cases.expected: Result string starts with "$6$" and contains a randomly generated 8‑character base‑64 salt after the prefix (e.g. "$6$AbCdEfGh$...")
cases.description: When the supplied salt is null the method must generate a random 8‑character salt and prepend the SHA‑512 prefix. The returned hash must therefore begin with "$6$" followed by the random salt and a trailing "$" before the hash data.

cases.expected: Result string starts with "$6$" and contains a random 8‑character salt; the hash part is still produced (non‑null).
cases.description: Even if the password byte array is empty the method should still produce a valid SHA‑512‑crypt string with a random salt.

cases.expected: Result string equals "$6$mysalt$" + a deterministic 86‑character hash (e.g. "$6$mysalt$KjG9rV...$"), i.e. the returned value is always the same for the same inputs.
cases.description: When a non‑null salt that already contains the SHA‑512 prefix is supplied, the method must use it unchanged and produce a deterministic hash. The returned string must start with the exact salt "$6$mysalt$".

cases.expected: Result string starts with "$6$mysalt$" (the method will prepend the missing prefix automatically).
cases.description: If the caller supplies a salt without the required "$6$" prefix, the internal sha2Crypt routine still receives the raw salt; the public method does not modify it, so the resulting hash will contain the raw salt after the prefix added by sha2Crypt. The test verifies that the final string contains "$6$mysalt$".

cases.expected: Result string starts with "$6$$" (i.e. an empty salt between the two dollar signs).
cases.description: An empty string is a valid (though unusual) salt. The method should forward it unchanged, resulting in a hash that begins with "$6$$".

cases.expected: Result string starts with "$6$$" (the provided salt contains only the prefix, no actual salt characters).
cases.description: When the supplied salt consists solely of the prefix, the implementation must handle the empty salt part correctly.

cases.expected: NullPointerException is thrown
cases.description: The method does not guard against a null password byte array; a NPE should be propagated from the underlying MessageDigest usage.

cases.expected: Result string starts with "$6$rounds=5000$mysalt$" followed by a deterministic 86‑character hash (the full string length is 108 characters).
cases.description: The salt contains a valid rounds specification; the method must honour the rounds value and include it in the output prefix.

cases.expected: Result string starts with "$6$rounds=10000$$" (i.e. an empty salt after the rounds specifier) followed by a deterministic hash.
cases.description: A rounds specifier is provided but no actual salt characters; the implementation should treat the salt part as empty and still produce a valid hash.

cases.expected: IllegalArgumentException is thrown (wrong algorithm prefix – SHA‑256 prefix used with SHA‑512 method).
cases.description: The salt starts with "$5$" which is the SHA‑256 prefix; sha512Crypt must reject it.

cases.expected: IllegalArgumentException is thrown (salt contains illegal character '!').
cases.description: Salt may only contain characters from the crypt base‑64 alphabet (A‑Z, a‑z, 0‑9, '.' and '/'). The exclamation mark is invalid.

cases.expected: IllegalArgumentException is thrown (salt length exceeds the maximum of 16 characters).
cases.description: The implementation limits the raw salt to 16 characters; a longer salt must be rejected.

cases.expected: Result string starts with "$6$unicode$" and is deterministic for the given Unicode password.
cases.description: Ensures that the method correctly handles UTF‑8 encoded passwords containing non‑ASCII characters.

cases.expected: Two consecutive calls with the same arguments return exactly the same string.
cases.description: Verifies that sha512Crypt is pure (no hidden state) and produces a repeatable result for identical inputs.

cases.expected: Result string starts with "$6$mysalt$$" (double dollar sign) followed by a deterministic hash.
cases.description: When the supplied salt already ends with a dollar sign, the implementation should treat the salt part as empty after the delimiter and still generate a valid hash.

cases.expected: IllegalArgumentException is thrown (rounds value is not a number)
cases.description: The salt contains a rounds specifier with a non‑numeric value. The implementation must detect the malformed rounds part and reject the salt.

cases.expected: IllegalArgumentException is thrown (missing rounds number)
cases.description: The rounds specifier is present but the numeric part is omitted. The method should treat this as an invalid salt pattern.

cases.expected: IllegalArgumentException is thrown (rounds value below minimum of 1000)
cases.description: The rounds number is smaller than the allowed lower bound (1000). The method must reject such a salt.

cases.expected: IllegalArgumentException is thrown (rounds value above maximum of 999999999)
cases.description: The rounds number exceeds the permitted upper bound. The implementation should throw an IllegalArgumentException.

cases.expected: IllegalArgumentException is thrown (salt contains a null character)
cases.description: The salt includes the Unicode null character (U+0000), which is not part of the allowed crypt base‑64 alphabet. The method must reject it.

cases.expected: IllegalArgumentException is thrown (salt contains whitespace)
cases.description: Whitespace is not allowed in the crypt salt. Supplying a space should cause the method to throw an IllegalArgumentException.
